record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.context_brief: Morphological PDE schemes as neural-network layers
record.original_question: Which numerical schemes for morphological partial differential equations are relevant for learning morphological operators or other nonlinear layers in deep-learning pipelines, how should the iterative nature of the approximations be handled, and can numerical schemes for morphological PDEs of matrix fields be used to learn nonlinearities for symmetric positive definite matrices or other matrix-valued data in Riemannian deep learning?

evidence.quote: What numerical schemes for morphological PDEs are relevant in order to learn morphological operators or another non-linear layer? How to deal with the iterative nature of the approximations? Can the numerical schemes for morphological PDEs of matrix fields be used to learn non-linearities for SPD, or other matrices, in Riemannian deep learning?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In mathematical morphology, the basic operators of flat dilation and erosion of a scalar image $u_0:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ by a structuring element associated with a convex function admit a partial differential equation (PDE) formulation. For example, dilation/erosion by balls of radius $t$ correspond to the Hamilton–Jacobi PDEs
$$\partial_t u = \pm\|\nabla u\|,\qquad u(\cdot,0)=u_0,$$
whose viscosity solutions $u(\cdot,t)$ realize the morphological operator at scale $t$. Solving such PDEs numerically requires specialized upwind, Rouy–Tourin, Osher–Sethian, or high-accuracy predictor–corrector schemes, and the schemes have been extended to fields of symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices $U_0:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathrm{Sym}^+(d)$ by exploiting the eigenstructure of symmetric matrices to define matrix-valued dilation/erosion.

In a deep-learning pipeline, a layer $L_\theta$ is a (typically differentiable) parametric mapping between feature tensors. A morphological layer is one whose forward pass approximates a dilation, erosion, or related nonlinear morphological operator (with learnable structuring function or shape parameters), so that gradients with respect to the parameters can be computed via backpropagation through the discretized PDE solver.

Problem. Address the following three questions.

(a) Identify which numerical schemes for the scalar morphological PDEs (upwind finite-difference, Rouy–Tourin, Engquist–Osher, semi-Lagrangian, predictor–corrector, etc.) are best suited to be embedded as layers $L_\theta$ in a deep network so that:
 (i) the forward pass faithfully approximates a parametric dilation/erosion or other nonlinear morphological operator, and
 (ii) the discrete scheme is differentiable (or admits a tractable subgradient) with respect to both the input feature tensor and the learnable parameters $\theta$ of the structuring function.

(b) Each such scheme is iterative: a target scale $t$ is reached by composing $K=t/\Delta t$ explicit time steps under a CFL-type constraint. Determine how this iterative structure should be handled inside a learnable layer—e.g., by fixing $K$, by using implicit/unrolled iterations, by adaptive time stepping, by deep-equilibrium-style fixed points, or by training-time vs. inference-time scheme switching—so that training is stable and the layer remains expressive.

(c) Let $U:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathrm{Sym}^+(d)$ be an SPD-matrix field and consider matrix-valued morphological PDEs of the form
$$\partial_t U = \pm\,\mathcal{F}(\nabla U),$$
where $\mathcal{F}$ is built from the spectral decomposition of the matrix gradient so as to preserve positive definiteness. Decide whether existing numerical schemes for such matrix-field morphological PDEs can be turned into layers of a Riemannian deep network operating on SPD-valued data (or other structured matrix-valued data) so as to provide nonlinear activations that respect the SPD geometry, and characterize what theoretical guarantees (preservation of positive definiteness, equivariance, stability under the chosen Riemannian metric) such layers can offer.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction. While individual ingredients exist—numerical schemes for scalar and matrix-field morphological PDEs (e.g., Burgeth et al.) and Riemannian SPD networks (Huang & Van Gool and follow-ups such as DreamNet)—no published work appears to combine differentiable morphological-PDE solvers as learnable layers for SPD/matrix-valued Riemannian deep learning, so the combined questions remain open.

status_evidence.title: PDE-based Morphology for Matrix Fields: Numerical Solution Schemes
status_evidence.snippet: Matrix-valued extension of nonlinear morphological PDEs for dilation and erosion with upwind and predictor-corrector numerical schemes for SPD matrix fields.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical schemes for matrix-field morphological PDEs exist but are not yet integrated as learnable deep-learning layers.

status_evidence.title: A Riemannian Network for SPD Matrix Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Deep network with bilinear mapping, eigenvalue rectification, and log layers for SPD inputs, trained via SGD on Stiefel manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Riemannian SPD deep networks use eigenvalue-based nonlinearities, but not morphological-PDE-derived ones.
